judge.notes: The front page uses a warm cream background with a serif face, bold titles, and small-caps metadata that stays visibly quieter than titles, giving a distinct newspaper-like point of view. Two columns with a rule divider and numbered entries make 30 stories skimmable at 1280px, though the page ends at about 1300px leaving a large empty area below. At 375px the single column works but metadata wraps awkwardly ('com-ments' breaks, orphaned words), and the nav wraps onto a second line. The thread page has clear nesting via left rules and indentation, but the depth lines are faint and the body text is long-measure at full width, reducing comfort.

The front page is dense and very compact, with monospace type that reads clearly, but the line height is tight and the metadata sits inline with titles so it competes with them; wrapped meta lines break awkwardly (e.g. 'comments' orphaned on the next line). The thread page shows nesting via indented left rules, which makes depth visible, though the comment text is a long undifferentiated column with little spacing between comments. Palette is restrained cream and brown with a single accent, which feels intentional and news-like. The 375px front page reflows acceptably but gets long and cramped, with metadata wrapping into ragged lines.
